name: Earth science: monthly Mauna Loa CO2 forecasts
description: Fit a forecast model of atmospheric CO2 on the Mauna Loa monthly record up to 1999, together with an ENSO index, and for every month from 2000 to 2024 forecast the next 12 monthly means using only data up to that month. The score is the mean root-mean-square error over the 12 lead times.

sources.locator: Betts et al. (2016): forecasting the annual rise of Mauna Loa CO2 from emissions and ENSO (the record 2015/16 rise).
Betts et al. (2018): verification of that operational CO2-rise forecast.
NOAA GML monthly mean CO2 at Mauna Loa (Scripps data before May 1974), March 1958 to December 2025; retrieved 2026-10-10; freely available under the GML data-use statement.
NOAA ERSSTv5 monthly SST used for the relative Nino 3.4 input (no constraints on use).

requirements.datasets: Derived from pinned public sources by python3 scripts/prepare_earth.py (hashes in catalog/earth-data-lock.json).

evaluation.benchmark: Earth science: monthly Mauna Loa CO2 forecasts
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: fit_co2_model(training) -> model; model.forecast(history) -> float array (12,) of monthly mean atmospheric CO2 at Mauna Loa (ppm, NOAA GML/SIO record) for each of the 12 months after the last month in history. training and history are dicts of numpy arrays over consecutive months from 1958-03: year, month, co2_ppm, measured_days (number of measurement days; -1 for interpolated months and for the 1958-1974 Scripps values) and relative_nino34 (ERSSTv5 Nino 3.4 anomaly minus the 20S-20N mean SST anomaly, from 1951-1980 monthly climatologies). training ends in 1999-12. Forecasts are then requested in order for every origin month from 2000-01 to 2024-12; history holds all months up to and including the origin month and nothing later. The candidate runs in a separate sandboxed process (numpy, scipy, scikit-learn and pandas importable; no file, network or subprocess access; one thread) with 120 s of CPU time for fitting and all predictions together; seed any randomness so that results are deterministic. Score: mean over leads 1-12 of the root-mean-square error (ppm) over the 300 origins, using only measured (not interpolated) verifying months; lower is better. Wrong shapes, NaN or values outside [250, 600] ppm are invalid

limitations: Only the CO2 record and an ENSO index are given; operational forecasts also use fossil-fuel emission estimates, so scores are not comparable with them.

Monthly means carry weather-driven noise of a few tenths of a ppm, and December 2022 - July 2023 values come from Maunakea after the Mauna Loa eruption; differences of a few hundredths of a ppm between candidates are not meaningful.
The 300 origins overlap strongly, so the effective sample is about 25 annual growth anomalies.

The GML file is rewritten monthly and old values are revised (ten monthly means of 1974-2014 changed by 0.01 ppm between the files of October and November 2026), so preparation uses the Internet Archive capture of the retrieved file that the data lock names. The ENSO index comes from the live ERSSTv5 file; if its values up to 2024 are revised, the derived-file hash check fails and the data must be re-recorded.
A better score is a better statistical forecast on these years, not a scientific discovery; the record is public, so search feedback can overfit it.

The candidate runs in a sandboxed child process that never receives months after a forecast origin, and no statement of the candidate is executed in the evaluator's process; outside macOS (kernel sandbox) deliberately hostile native code could bypass the file policy.

state_of_the_art.statement: No published value exists for this protocol. The evaluator's reference, seasonal persistence plus the last 12-month increase, scores 0.708 ppm; the seed, a 10-year quadratic trend with two annual harmonics refitted at every origin, 0.699 ppm.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Forecast the near-term rise of atmospheric CO2, whose year-to-year variations reflect the response of land carbon sinks to climate variability such as ENSO.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Year-ahead CO2 forecasts test understanding of the carbon-cycle response to climate variability and give an early check on whether emissions and sinks behave as expected.

papers.title: El Nino and a record CO2 rise
papers.primary_goal: Forecast the annual rise of Mauna Loa CO2 from emissions and the ENSO forecast.
papers.task_relation: The task scores monthly Mauna Loa CO2 forecasts at 1-12 months from the record and an ENSO index on held-out years.

papers.title: A successful prediction of the record CO2 rise associated with the 2015/2016 El Nino
papers.primary_goal: Verify the operational forecast of the 2016 CO2 rise.
papers.task_relation: Same forecast target and verification against the Mauna Loa record.

science_relevance.reason: Both cited papers have forecasting the Mauna Loa CO2 rise as their main goal, the problem the local task scores; no reproduction of their numbers is claimed.
science_relevance.verification_basis: Crossref metadata checked on 2026-10-10; the GML file header (data use, interpolation flags, Maunakea period) read; evaluator run on the pinned data.
